steps.description: pattern = s + "#" + (s reversed) = "aacecaaa#aaacecaa". The lps value at its last letter is the longest prefix of s that reads the same backwards - the '#' stops a match from running past s.
pattern[1] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[1] = 1.
pattern[2] = 'c' breaks the 1-letter match; try the next shorter candidate, length 0 (lps[0]).
pattern[2] = 'c' starts no prefix: lps[2] = 0.
pattern[3] = 'e' starts no prefix: lps[3] = 0.
pattern[4] = 'c' starts no prefix: lps[4] = 0.
pattern[5] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[5] = 1.
pattern[6] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[6] = 2.
pattern[7] = 'a' breaks the 2-letter match; try the next shorter candidate, length 1 (lps[1]).
pattern[7] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[7] = 2.
pattern[8] = '#' breaks the 2-letter match; try the next shorter candidate, length 1 (lps[1]).
pattern[8] = '#' breaks the 1-letter match; try the next shorter candidate, length 0 (lps[0]).
pattern[8] = '#' starts no prefix: lps[8] = 0.
pattern[9] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[9] = 1.
pattern[10] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[10] = 2.
pattern[11] = 'a' breaks the 2-letter match; try the next shorter candidate, length 1 (lps[1]).
pattern[11] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[11] = 2.
pattern[12] = 'c' continues the matched prefix: lps[12] = 3.
pattern[13] = 'e' continues the matched prefix: lps[13] = 4.
pattern[14] = 'c' continues the matched prefix: lps[14] = 5.
pattern[15] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[15] = 6.
pattern[16] = 'a' continues the matched prefix: lps[16] = 7.
lps[last] = 7, so s[0..6] = "aacecaa" is already a palindrome. Put the reverse of the rest, "a", in front: "aaacecaaa".
